action: VW ID. owners: install the available software update (3.9.1 over the air for cars below 4.0; workshop visit above 4.0), and never accept an unknown Bluetooth pairing request.
date_note: Date of the heise report; the flaw was reported in 2024 and the fix released about three weeks ago
exec: Connected-car flaws affect owners' privacy; Volkswagen says a fix is out and no recall is planned.
plain: Researchers showed that older Volkswagen infotainment systems could be listened to and tracked over Bluetooth after a pairing was accepted. VW says a software update is now available.
summary: heise reports that PCA Cyber Security researchers showed older VW infotainment systems could be eavesdropped on and tracked via Bluetooth (the PerfektBlue flaws in BlueSDK) once a pairing was accepted. VW says the fix has been available for about three weeks, with no recall planned and no driving-safety effect. The Times, cited by heise, says several hundred thousand cars may be affected.
title: Volkswagen patches Bluetooth flaws that allowed eavesdropping and tracking in older cars
